description: Detection/non-detection of six amphibian species (boreal chorus frog, boreal toad, columbia spotted frog, northern leopard frog, western tiger salamander, wood frog) at 333 wetland sites in 71 catchments of two national forests in Wyoming and Colorado, 2012-2019 (Rocky Mountain Amphibian Project), 1-8 surveys per site-year, with site area, isolation metrics, coordinates, survey date, observer count and surveyor type; the species list differs by forest (__survey_taxa).
reference: Addis, B. (2026). Rocky Mountain Amphibian Project occupancy data and analyses [Data set]. figshare.
notes: Replaces addis_2026_rmap_mbrt_dynocc and addis_2026_rmap_bt_dynocc (ruling #31). Squared air temperature from the wood frog file shipped as obs_air_temp_f_sq (Medicine Bow-Routt surveys only).

description: Detection histories of two West African crocodylians (Mecistops cataphractus, CR; Crocodylus suchus) from 195 nocturnal spotlight surveys on 3-5 consecutive nights at 42 sites in Côte d'Ivoire, 2014-2019, with per-survey environmental covariates.
reference: Ahizi, M. N., Kouman, C. Y., Ouattara, A., Kouamé, N. P., Dede, A., Fairet, E., & Shirley, M. H. (2021). Detectability and impact of repetitive surveys on threatened West African crocodylians. Ecology and Evolution, 11, 15325-15338.
notes: First crocodylian table. Encounter-rate and wariness files not shipped (derived ratios). No coordinates in source.

description: Invasive spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) in 48 plots at 12 New Jersey vineyards, two rounds in autumn 2019: three eDNA qPCR replicates of spray-aggregation samples plus the paired visual count of the same vines (multi-method, cluster_id = vineyard).
reference: Allen, M. C., Nielsen, A. L., Peterson, D. L., & Lockwood, J. L. (2021). Terrestrial eDNA survey outperforms conventional approach for detecting an invasive pest insect within an agricultural ecosystem. Environmental DNA. https://doi.org/10.1002/edn3.231
notes: Experimental E9 (multi-scale eDNA, multi-method): qPCR replicates as occasions 1-3, visual survey as occasion 4 (obs_method); period = round. Three suspected false positives flagged, not recoded.

description: Annual resighting histories (CJS / Pradel) of 4,608 breeding blue-footed boobies (Sula nebouxii) with sex, Isla Isabel, Mexico, 1991-2013 (Ancona et al. 2017).
reference: Ancona, S., Zuniga-Vega, J. J., Rodriguez, C., & Drummond, H. (2017). Long-term population dynamics reveal that survival and recruitment of tropical boobies improve after a hurricane. Journal of Avian Biology 48(2), 320-332.
notes: Dryad version zip (version 9171), one MARK-format file; sex from the two group columns (1 0 male, 0 1 female, per the Dryad file description). No band numbers: unit = line number.

description: Presence/absence of the invasive aquatic plant Hydrilla verticillata in 506 James River rock pools (Richmond, Virginia) over 4,211 irregularly timed surveys, 2017-2021, with pool size, flooding and distance covariates; dynamic occupancy (years as periods).
reference: Armstrong, J., et al. (2024). Regional and local factors interact to shape colonization and extinction dynamics of invasive Hydrilla verticillata in a patchy landscape. Ecology and Evolution, 14, e11558.
notes: Dryad version zip. Duplicated pool-date rows collapsed to one visit (12 conflicting, y = 1). Distance-to-occupied-pool and transition probabilities not shipped (derived from detections).

description: Robust-design photo-ID capture histories of 205 marked juvenile/adult bottlenose dolphins off the east coast of Scotland, 27 field seasons (1989-2015) x 3-5 monthly secondary occasions; y = sighted; sex and the season it was determined as covariates (rebuilding the authors' multistate histories).
reference: Arso Civil, M., Cheney, B., Quick, N. J., Islas-Villanueva, V., Graves, J. A., Janik, V. M., Thompson, P. M., & Hammond, P. S. (2019). Variations in age- and sex-specific survival rates help explain population trend in a discrete marine mammal population. Ecology and Evolution, 9(1), 533-544.
notes: Built from the RMark input files in the Dryad version zip. The multistate file is a recode of this table (asserted); the adults-only file is a restriction; calves are the sibling table arsocivil_2019_scotland_dolphincalf_cjs.

description: Annual sighting histories of 56 bottlenose dolphin calves of known mother and birth year off the east coast of Scotland, 26 years (1990-2015); y = sighted; for age-specific CJS survival in the first three years of life; the deposit's two (unlabelled) MARK groups as a covariate.
reference: Arso Civil, M., Cheney, B., Quick, N. J., Islas-Villanueva, V., Graves, J. A., Janik, V. M., Thompson, P. M., & Hammond, P. S. (2019). Variations in age- and sex-specific survival rates help explain population trend in a discrete marine mammal population. Ecology and Evolution, 9(1), 533-544.
notes: Sibling of arsocivil_2019_scotland_dolphin_rd (same deposit). Group columns unlabelled in the deposit (first-born vs subsequent per the paper).

description: Camera-trap detection of leopard and spotted hyaena in 3-day occasions at 36 stations in Omo National Park, Ethiopia, 2021, with habitat and distance covariates.
reference: Asfaw, T., Sillero-Zubiri, C., Leirs, H., Gebresenbet, F., & Bauer, H. (2025). Anthropogenic and environmental factors determine occupancy and rarity of large carnivores in the Omo Valley, southwest Ethiopia. Ecological Solutions and Evidence.
notes: Dryad version zip; Omo NP only (CCNP matrices have no survey year); prey abundance columns not shipped.

description: Multi-state capture histories (0 not captured, 1 spawner, 2 non-spawner) of 21,430 tagged anadromous Dolly Varden (Salvelinus malma) in five western Canadian Arctic rivers, falls 2007-2020 (river-specific spans), with sex.
reference: Banik, A., Gallagher, C., Howland, K., Lea, E., Dillon, F., McLeod, R., Muthukumarana, S., & Cowen, L. (2025). Assessing the effects of changes in reproductive condition on the survival of anadromous Dolly Varden (Salvelinus malma) using Bayesian multistate capture-recapture modelling. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences.
notes: Five rivers in one table (unit_river); deposited matrices without tag ids; Rat River capture/breeding discrepancy (10 cells) resolved to the breeding matrix.

description: Precise-location sibling without Carcharodus baeticus and Polyommatus golgus: counts of 100 butterfly species on 1,725 Pollard walks of 22 transects (700-3,100 m a.s.l.) of the Sierra Nevada Global-Change Observatory, Spain, March-October 2008-2020, summed over the sections of each walk, with pseudonymous observer team, start and end time, wind, cloud cover and temperature.
reference: Barea-Azcón J M (2021). Dataset of butterfly monitoring in Sierra Nevada (Spain). Version 1.2. Sierra Nevada Global-Change Observatory (UGR-JA). Sampling event dataset.
notes: Zeros from the walk list (parent events, 109 with no butterfly). Sections summed. Genus- and family-level records not shipped. No walks in 2011. E7.3 sibling of barea_2021_sierranevada_butterfly_count without the IUCN-threatened species, locations as published.

description: Counts of 102 butterfly species on 1,725 Pollard walks of 22 transects (700-3,100 m a.s.l.) of the Sierra Nevada Global-Change Observatory, Spain, March-October 2008-2020, summed over the sections of each walk, with pseudonymous observer team, start and end time, wind, cloud cover and temperature.
reference: Barea-Azcón J M (2021). Dataset of butterfly monitoring in Sierra Nevada (Spain). Version 1.2. Sierra Nevada Global-Change Observatory (UGR-JA). Sampling event dataset.
notes: Zeros from the walk list (parent events, 109 with no butterfly). Sections summed. Genus- and family-level records not shipped. No walks in 2011. Locations coarsened; barea_2021_sierran_butterfly_exact_count has the unthreatened species at published precision.

description: Side scan sonar counts of adult Green Sturgeon (Acipenser medirostris) in 70 pools of the upper Sacramento River, California, 2020-2022: 3 to 7 passes per pool per year; 2022 passes also recounted for fish >= 1.5 m.
reference: Battaile, B., Mora, E., Lehman, B. & Dudley, P. Estimating spawning Green Sturgeon (Acipenser medirostris) abundance using side scan sonar and N-mixture models. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1139/cjfas-2023-0228
notes: Pools not geolocated (by the source). 2022 size-filtered recount and pass direction as obs covariates.

description: Camera-trap distance sampling of mountain hares (Lepus timidus) at Holme Moss, Peak District, winter 2017-18: 91 cameras at six 1 km sites, night-time 1 s snapshot detections in twelve 1 m radial-distance bins per camera, with seconds deployed as effort and hares per bin. 3,706 detections. First camera-trap distance-sampling table; one of three sibling tables comparing survey methods.
reference: Bedson, C. P. E., Thomas, L., Wheeler, P. M., Reid, N., Harris, W. E., Lloyd, H., Mallon, D., & Preziosi, R. (2021). Estimating density of mountain hares using distance sampling: a comparison of daylight visual surveys, night-time thermal imaging and camera traps. Wildlife Biology, 2021(3), wlb.00802.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): camera-trap distance sampling, occasion = 1 m radial bin, snapshotInterval 1 s, effort in seconds. Sibling tables: _vis_ds, _therm_ds.

description: Night-time thermal-imaging point-transect distance sampling of mountain hares (Lepus timidus) at Holme Moss, Peak District, winter 2017-18: 114 visits to 71 vantage points at six 1 km sites, hare groups in eight radial-distance bins (50 m to 350 m, then 350-750 m) per visit, with hares per bin. 206 detections. One of three sibling tables comparing survey methods.
reference: Bedson, C. P. E., Thomas, L., Wheeler, P. M., Reid, N., Harris, W. E., Lloyd, H., Mallon, D., & Preziosi, R. (2021). Estimating density of mountain hares using distance sampling: a comparison of daylight visual surveys, night-time thermal imaging and camera traps. Wildlife Biology, 2021(3), wlb.00802.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = radial-distance bin (point transect). Visits recovered from row order (matches the paper's replicate counts). Processor-binned distances. Sibling tables: _vis_ds, _cam_ds.

description: Daylight line-transect distance sampling of mountain hares (Lepus timidus) at six 1 km sites on Holme Moss, Peak District, winter 2017-18: hare groups in five perpendicular-distance bins (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20-100, 100-400 m) per site walk, with walk length and hares per bin. 41 detections. One of three sibling tables comparing survey methods.
reference: Bedson, C. P. E., Thomas, L., Wheeler, P. M., Reid, N., Harris, W. E., Lloyd, H., Mallon, D., & Preziosi, R. (2021). Estimating density of mountain hares using distance sampling: a comparison of daylight visual surveys, night-time thermal imaging and camera traps. Wildlife Biology, 2021(3), wlb.00802.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = distance bin. Continuous distances binned by the processor to the paper's breaks plus a 100-400 m bin. Six walks only. Sibling tables: _therm_ds, _cam_ds.

description: Repeated counts of two endemic Colombian birds (Capito hypoleucus, Habia gutturalis) at 70 point counts in fragmented Andean forest around two hydroelectric impoundments in Antioquia, two visits a year in 2014 and 2015, with landscape, weather and nest-predation covariates; coordinates coarsened.
reference: Betancur, J. S., Morales-Rozo, A., & Parra, J. L. (2021). Occupancy of the Sooty Ant-Tanager (Habia gutturalis) and White-Mantled Barbet (Capito hypoleucus) in fragmented forests of the Central Andes in Colombia. Ornitología Colombiana, e383.
notes: Counts bound to points by row order (as the authors' scripts); coordinates coarsened (source calls both species endangered).

description: Daily camera-trap detection/non-detection of Asiatic black bear at 67 camera sites in two Himachal Pradesh wildlife sanctuaries (Rupi Bhaba 2019, Daranghati 2018), up to 49 camera-days each; 58 detections in 2,326 camera-days; no coordinates.
reference: Bhattacharya, A., Chatterjee, N., Angrish, K., Meena, D., Sinha, B. C. & Habib, B. (2022). Population estimation of Asiatic black bear in the Himalayan Region of India using camera traps. Ursus 33(e8), 1-10.
notes: Two protected areas sampled in different years, shipped as one table with cluster_id = area. Camera-relative day occasions, no dates. Paper paywalled; abstract used.

description: Daily detection/non-detection of the Alpine mountain hare at 46 camera-trap stations (1,227-2,740 m) in the Mont-Blanc massif, France, September 2017 to June 2022, binned into 20 meteorological seasons, with surveyed camera-days from setup dates minus deposited downtime windows, station coordinates, elevation, slope, aspect, habitat and six vegetation-cover classes.
reference: Bison, M., Yoccoz, N. G., Carlson, B. Z., Bayle, A., & Delestrade, A. (2024). Camera traps reveal seasonal variation in activity and occupancy of the Alpine mountain hare Lepus timidus varronis. Wildlife Biology, 2024(4), e01186.
notes: Record-table source (contact days) plus a camera table with setup dates and downtime windows but no end dates: survey set inferred to 2022-06-30 (abstract). Season binning is the processor's; the paper's occasion and season definitions were not reachable. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Weekly counts of independent grey wolf and brown bear camera-trap detections at 229 deployments (2009-2023) in and around Sarikamis-Allahuekber Mountains National Park, northeastern Turkiye, up to 104 seven-day occasions per deployment, with camera, topographic, land-cover, distance and human-activity covariates.
reference: Blount, J. D., Green, A. M., Chynoweth, M., Coban, E., Kusak, J. & Sekercioglu, C. H. (2025). Combining N-mixture and occupancy analysis offers a more complete picture of carnivore habitat use in Northeastern Turkiye. PLOS One 20(5), e0320768.
notes: Matrices have no row ids; aligned to the covariate sheet by row order (229 each). 13 deployments have no surveyed week. Lynx counts not alignable (215 x 472); lynx 0/1 in blount_2025_neturkiye_lynx_occ.

description: Eurasian lynx detection / non-detection per seven-day occasion at 229 camera deployments (2009-2023) in and around Sarikamis-Allahuekber Mountains National Park, northeastern Turkiye, with camera, topographic, land-cover, distance and human-activity covariates; sibling of the wolf and bear count table.
reference: Blount, J. D., Green, A. M., Chynoweth, M., Coban, E., Kusak, J. & Sekercioglu, C. H. (2025). Combining N-mixture and occupancy analysis offers a more complete picture of carnivore habitat use in Northeastern Turkiye. PLOS One 20(5), e0320768.
notes: 0/1 only: the lynx count matrix (215 x 472, no ids) cannot be aligned to the deployments. Same survey set as blount_2025_neturkiye_carniv_count.

description: Bumble bee counts (females, males, queens) for 15 species and species-group classes, including the endangered rusty patched bumble bee, from five one-hour active searches at 25 sites across Minnesota, June-September 2021, with survey weather, bloom and honey bee covariates and site land use; coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree.
reference: Boone, M. (2023). 2021 Minnesota bumble bee survey data. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.0p2ngf264
notes: Taxa are identification classes as recorded, two of them species aggregates. Coordinates coarsened and site ids replaced for B. affinis; boone_2023_minnesota_bombus_exact_count has the other classes at published precision.

description: Bumble bee counts (females, males, queens) for 14 species and species-group classes (all but the endangered rusty patched bumble bee) from five one-hour active searches at 25 sites across Minnesota, June-September 2021, with survey weather, bloom and honey bee covariates and site land use; coordinates as published.
reference: Boone, M. (2023). 2021 Minnesota bumble bee survey data. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.0p2ngf264
notes: E7.3 sibling of boone_2023_minnesota_bombus_count without B. affinis; coordinates and site names as published.

description: Pitfall-trap presence / absence of 115 beetle taxa in five fortnightly collections at 60 farmland woodlands of known age (England and Scotland, 2013-2014), with trap numbers, woodland age, area, structure and landscape history.
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: Species-year NA cells (taxa never caught that year) shipped as 0 with y_raw = NA, as in the authors' code; one lost collection has no rows. Siblings: _bird_comm, _mammal_comm, _plant_comm.

description: Bird presence / absence (54 species) on up to three repeat surveys at 125 farmland woodlands of known age in England and Scotland (2015, 2017), with surveyor, date, woodland age, area, structure and landscape history.
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: 47 surveys not carried out have no rows. Siblings: _beetle_comm, _mammal_comm, _plant_comm.

description: Small-mammal live-trap presence / absence (four species) on four trap days at 100 farmland woodlands of known age in England and Scotland (2013-2014), with woodland age, area, structure and landscape history.
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: Complete matrix. Siblings: _beetle_comm, _bird_comm, _plant_comm.

description: Single-survey presence / absence of 200 vascular plant species at 129 farmland woodlands of known age in England and Scotland, with woodland age, area, structure and landscape history (no repeat visits).
reference: Bradfer-Lawrence, T., Dobson, A., Finch, T., et al. (2025). Data and code for "Spillovers and legacies of land management on temperate woodland biodiversity". Zenodo.
notes: Single visit per site (n_occasions = 1): detection not estimable from this table. Survey dates not deposited. Siblings: _beetle_comm, _bird_comm, _mammal_comm.

description: Search-encounter spatial capture-recapture of cheetahs in the Maasai Mara, Kenya: animal x 1-km search pixel x day over eight 90-day sessions in and out of the wildebeest migration, 2015-2018, with km driven per pixel-day; session-scoped ids; pixel coordinates centred (VU taxon).
reference: Broekhuis, F., Elliot, N. B., Keiwua, K., Koinet, K., Macdonald, D. W., Mogensen, N., Thuo, D., & Gopalaswamy, A. M. (2021). Resource pulses influence the spatio-temporal dynamics of a large carnivore population. Ecography, 44(3), 358-369.
original_license: CC0 1.0 (Dryad; ReadMe asks re-users to contact the authors)
notes: Search-encounter SCR; effort table = pixel-day operation matrix with log km driven. IUCN VU; coordinates centred.

description: Adult monarch counts on IMMP transects, three surveys per summer at 60 Wisconsin grassland sites in 2018 and 2019 (352 surveys), with nectar-species richness and milkweed density per survey, site coordinates and patch/landscape metrics.
reference: Bruce, A.S., Thogmartin, W.E., Trosen, C., Oberhauser, K., & Gratton, C. (2022). Landscape- and local-level variables affect monarchs in Midwest grasslands. Landscape Ecology, 37, 93-108.
notes: Survey dates not deposited. Egg/larva per-stem ratios not shipped.

description: Camera-trap detection / non-detection of fishers at 64 sites x 64 sampling occasions, Alberta, 2016; the unmarked data set paired with the genetic SCR table burgar_2018_alberta_fisher_scr.
reference: Burgar, J. M., Stewart, F. E. C., Volpe, J. P., Fisher, J. T., & Burton, A. C. (2018). Estimating density for species conservation: Comparing camera trap spatial count models to genetic spatial capture-recapture models. Global Ecology and Conservation, 15, e00411.
notes: Single-species camera detections, complete 64 x 64 matrix. No coordinates (site numbering not keyed to the TDF). Occasion length only in the paywalled-to-agents paper.

description: Genetic spatial capture-recapture detections of 24 fishers at 64 hair-snag sites over 4 occasions in Alberta, 2016 (one row per fisher x site x occasion), with UTM site coordinates in __traps.
reference: Burgar, J. M., Stewart, F. E. C., Volpe, J. P., Fisher, J. T., & Burton, A. C. (2018). Estimating density for species conservation: Comparing camera trap spatial count models to genetic spatial capture-recapture models. Global Ecology and Conservation, 15, e00411.
notes: Closed-population genetic SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps. Survey set = TDF usage (all sites, all occasions). Sibling camera table burgar_2018_alberta_fisher_count not joinable (different site numbering). Below floor (24 individuals).

description: Annual capture histories of 11,919 yellow-bellied toads in four French populations (two in harvested woodland, two riverine), 2000-2014, with birth year where known.
reference: Cayuela, H., Lemaitre, J.-F., Bonnaire, E., Pichenot, J., & Schmidt, B. R. (2020). Population position along the fast-slow life-history continuum predicts intraspecific variation in actuarial senescence. Journal of Animal Ecology, 89.
notes: Dryad version zip; four sheets stacked with population as cluster_id; rows start at birth year where it is later than the study start.

description: Annual capture histories of 1,553 marked diamondback terrapins (Malaclemys terrapin) on the Kiawah River, South Carolina, across 28 sampling years 1983-2012, pooled from 3,376 seine, net, hand and crab-pot captures; sex, first site, captures per year and crab-pot captures per year.
reference: Cecala, K. (2026). Long-term diamondback terrapin capture-recapture data from Kiawah Island, South Carolina (1983-2012). Dryad.
notes: Survey years inferred from capture records (2000-2001 have none). Radio relocations and unmarked animals excluded. IUCN VU species; no coordinates in source.

description: Multi-state closed robust design capture histories of 209 photo-identified Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops aduncus) at three sites in Perth metropolitan waters, Western Australia: 16 seasonal primary periods (June 2011 to May 2015) x 3-6 secondary occasions; y is the site of capture (0 not captured, 1 estuary, 2 embayment, 3 open coast). The Program MARK input for Chabanne et al. (2017) Scenario 1.
reference: Chabanne, D.B.H., Pollock, K.H., Finn, H., Bejder, L. & Gimenez, O. (2017). Applying the multistate capture-recapture robust design to characterize metapopulation structure. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 8(11), 1547-1557.
notes: Season layout of the 75 unlabelled MARK columns inferred against the thesis effort table (76 completed occasions); summer 2011-12 carries 4 columns. 2-state (Scenario 2) file not shipped. One duplicated id relabelled.

description: Field-identified detections of the endangered Shenandoah salamander and the red-backed salamander at 131 sites in Shenandoah National Park, 2011-2014 (2-5 surveys per year), with the joint field state and the DNA-confirmed identity where available: the worked example for two-species occupancy with misidentification.
reference: Chambert, T., Grant, E. H. C., Miller, D. A. W., Nichols, J. D., Mulder, K. P., & Brand, A. B. (2018). Two-species occupancy modelling accounting for species misidentification and non-detection. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(6), 1468-1477.
notes: First species-misidentification table: joint field state in y_raw, DNA confirmation in obs_dna_state. No coordinates deposited.

description: Alder flycatcher removal counts (individuals first detected in each of three 5-minute intervals) at 50 points in Massachusetts beaver meadows, 2005, survey 1, with woody vegetation, structure, time and date covariates (unmarked alfl.csv; Chandler, King & DeStefano 2009). First multinomial_cell table.
reference: Chandler, R. B., King, D. I. & DeStefano, S. (2009). Scrub-shrub bird habitat associations at multiple spatial scales in beaver meadows in Massachusetts. The Auk 126(1), 186-197.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package. occasion indexes the removal interval (standard E9 declared stretch); multinomialType = removal. Round-trip tested in converters/rt_03_alfl_removal.R.

description: Annual life-stage histories (multistate: not seen / one linear leaf / one rounded leaf / two-leaved adult / flower spike) of 218 marked Platanthera macrophylla orchids at Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest, 2011-2015, with leaf area per plant-year; source-inferred dormancy and death are y = 0 with the code kept.
reference: Cleavitt, N. L., Berry, E. J., Hautaniemi, J., & Fahey, T. J. (2017). Life stages, demographic rates, and leaf damage for the round-leaved orchids, Platanthera orbiculata (Pursh.) Lindley and P. macrophylla (Goldie) P.M. Brown in a northern hardwood forest in New Hampshire, USA. Botany, 95(1), 61-71.
notes: Sibling of cleavitt_2017_hbef_plaorb_ms (same census, one table per species under ruling #20). Fetched from the LTER DataONE member node (EDI PASTA refuses public reads). Lost flags censor the history; three undefined code-5 cells dropped.

description: Annual life-stage histories (multistate: not seen / one linear leaf / one rounded leaf / two-leaved adult / flower spike) of 241 marked Platanthera orbiculata orchids at Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest, 2011-2015, with leaf area per plant-year; source-inferred dormancy and death are y = 0 with the code kept.
reference: Cleavitt, N. L., Berry, E. J., Hautaniemi, J., & Fahey, T. J. (2017). Life stages, demographic rates, and leaf damage for the round-leaved orchids, Platanthera orbiculata (Pursh.) Lindley and P. macrophylla (Goldie) P.M. Brown in a northern hardwood forest in New Hampshire, USA. Botany, 95(1), 61-71.
notes: Sibling of cleavitt_2017_hbef_plamac_ms (same census, one table per species under ruling #20). Fetched from the LTER DataONE member node (EDI PASTA refuses public reads). Lost flags censor the history; three undefined code-5 cells dropped.

description: Daily detection/non-detection (with record counts in y_raw) of 35 bird and mammal taxa at 129 game cameras deployed about a week each at wildlife openings in the Monongahela National Forest, West Virginia, in April-May 2019, 2020 and 2021, with camera-hours per day as effort; one of three datasets behind a deer-coyote two-species occupancy paper.
reference: Clipp, H. L., Pesi, S. M., Miller, M. L., Gigliotti, L. C., Skelly, B. P., & Rota, C. T. (2024). White-tailed deer detection rates increase when coyotes are present. Ecology and Evolution, 14(3), e11149.
notes: Wildlife-openings dataset only. The deposit also re-uploads Snapshot USA 2020 (third-party, not hosted) and a Wildlife Insights export licensed CC BY-NC (shipped separately as clipp_2024_wvprivate_comm).

description: Daily detection/non-detection (with sequence counts in y_raw) of 47 bird and mammal taxa at 146 game cameras deployed about two months each on private land in three West Virginia county pairs in summer 2022, with camera-hours per day as effort, coordinates and detection distance; one of three datasets behind a deer-coyote two-species occupancy paper.
reference: Clipp, H. L., Pesi, S. M., Miller, M. L., Gigliotti, L. C., Skelly, B. P., & Rota, C. T. (2024). White-tailed deer detection rates increase when coyotes are present. Ecology and Evolution, 14(3), e11149.
original_license: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record) / CC BY-NC (licence column of sequences.csv)
notes: Wildlife Insights export; the per-row CC BY-NC governs over the record's CC BY. Eight deployments beyond the paper's 138 shipped and marked in __units. Coordinates on private land as published; unit ids pseudonymised (deposited names are landowner surnames).

description: Daily camera-trap detection of chimpanzees at 53 systematic and targeted cameras in the Issa Valley, Tanzania, March-December 2018.
reference: Crunchant, A.-S., Borchers, D., Kuehl, H., & Piel, A. K. (2020). Listening and watching: Do camera traps or acoustic sensors more efficiently detect wild chimpanzees in an open habitat? Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 11, 542-552.
notes: Dryad version zip; camera sheet only (acoustic sheet held); coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree (IUCN EN).

description: Annual spring capture histories of 158 female polar bear family units in Svalbard, 1992-2019, coded in 11 states by the female's age class or the number and age of her dependent offspring; capture dates per row.
reference: Cubaynes, S., Aars, J., Yoccoz, N. G., Pradel, R., Wiig, Ø., Ims, R. A., & Gimenez, O. (2021). Modeling the demography of species providing extended parental care: A capture-recapture multievent model with a case study on polar bears (Ursus maritimus). Ecology and Evolution, 11(7), 3380-3392.
notes: Multievent family-unit coding; known-age females start at age 2. Species IUCN VU; no coordinates in the deposit.

description: Repeated half-hour point counts of 182 bird species (waterbirds and others) at 14 points around Lake Ngami, Botswana, on six week-long field trips from October 2007 to June 2009 as the lake dried, with foraging / not foraging / flying-over splits and MODIS lake area; coordinates coarsened.

description: Annual census histories (1995-2022) of 4,042 tagged plants of the endangered Astragalus microcymbus in 30 plots in the Gunnison Basin, Colorado: observed stage (seedling, vegetative, reproductive, not seen); the source's inferred dormancy and death kept as y_raw.

description: Multi-state closed robust design histories of 1,970 tagged plants of the endangered Astragalus microcymbus in 28 plots in Colorado, 2013-2015: up to ten within-season visits per year, y = observed above-ground state (not found, vegetative, reproductive).

description: Counts of 14 riparian landbird species on 4,712 five-minute 50 m point counts at 183 stations on 13 riparian transects in protected areas of Marin County, California (1997-2019; normally two visits per breeding season), with explicit zeros as deposited by Point Blue Conservation Science.

description: Repeated hand-net counts (two visits by different observers per season) of four water beetles, including the Habitats Directive species Graphoderus bilineatus, at 337 locations in the Netherlands, each surveyed in one year of each six-year round 2011-2016 and 2017-2022 (de Zeeuw et al. 2024).
reference: de Zeeuw, M., van Strien, A., Koese, B., Stienstra, J., & Soldaat, L. (2024). Trends in abundance and occupancy of the protected waterbeetle Graphoderus bilineatus in the Netherlands. Journal of Insect Conservation.

description: Spatial capture-recapture detections of 29 identified jaguars at 20 camera stations over 183 days in Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary, Belize (Aug 2013 - Feb 2014), one row per jaguar x station x operating day, with the time of each photograph and station coordinates (UTM 16N) in __traps.
reference: Distiller, G. B., Borchers, D. L., Foster, R. J., & Harmsen, B. J. (2020). Using Continuous-Time Spatial Capture-Recapture models to make inference about animal activity patterns. Ecology and Evolution, 10(20), 11826-11837.
notes: Closed-population SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps. Survey set = deposited station x day operating matrix. Detection times kept in obs_capture_time for the continuous-time model. Unsexed individuals included with unit_sex = U.

description: Cormack-Jolly-Seber resight histories of colour-marked bicolored sweat bees (Agapostemon virescens) at garden and non-garden Echinacea patches in seven Boston-area community gardens, 16 survey days in July 2023, with patch impervious surface.
reference: Dooley, K. A., Murphy, A. W., & Crone, E. E. (2025). Landscape context affects both capture probability and abundance of solitary bees in cities. Ecological Applications, 35(6), e70099.
notes: Histories rebuilt from the raw captures and asserted equal to the deposited MARK file; 7 bees seen at both patches appear once per patch, as in the deposited file (README says excluded).

description: Detection/non-detection of 12 foliage-gleaning bird species on up to 3 replicate 10-minute point counts per year at 373 Hubbard Brook plots, 2010-2018, with elevation, coordinates (UTM 19N and WGS84), survey day and time (spOccupancy::hbefTrends; Doser et al. 2022 integrated community occupancy data). The package's hbef2015 is the 2015 slice.
reference: Doser, J. W., Leuenberger, W., Sillett, T. S., Hallworth, M. T. & Zipkin, E. F. (2022). Integrated community occupancy models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 13, 919-932. Package: Doser, Finley, Kery & Zipkin (2022) MEE 13, 1670-1678.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package (spOccupancy); the underlying EDI deposit (edi.348) is behind an access wall for the builder. 45 covariate-only cells not surveyed. hbef2015 not shipped separately (identical 2015 slice).

description: Time-removal detections of 12 foliage-gleaning bird species (first-detection interval of three 2-minute intervals) at 80 NEON point-count sites in Bartlett Experimental Forest, NH, June 2015, with elevation, coordinates, survey day and hour (spOccupancy::neon2015; Doser et al. 2022). Two species never detected.
reference: Doser, J. W., Leuenberger, W., Sillett, T. S., Hallworth, M. T. & Zipkin, E. F. (2022). Integrated community occupancy models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 13, 919-932. Package: Doser, Finley, Kery & Zipkin (2022) MEE 13, 1670-1678.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package (spOccupancy). Removal design on species detection (not individuals): occasion = 2-minute interval, multinomialType = removal; NA-after-detection in the package array shipped as 0.

description: Invasive rusty crayfish (Orconectes rusticus) in 12 upper-Midwest lakes, 2014: four eDNA qPCR replicates of water samples at alternate trap locations plus the paired overnight baited trap (multi-method, cluster_id = lake), with catches of two other crayfish species.
reference: Dougherty, M. M., Larson, E. R., Renshaw, M. A., Gantz, C. A., Egan, S. P., Erickson, D. M., & Lodge, D. M. (2016). Environmental DNA (eDNA) detects the invasive rusty crayfish Orconectes rusticus at low abundances. Journal of Applied Ecology, 53(3), 722-732.
notes: Experimental E9 (multi-scale eDNA, multi-method): qPCR replicates as occasions 1-4, baited trap as occasion 5 (obs_method). First freshwater invertebrate eDNA table.

description: Spatial capture-recapture of 24 Mojave desert tortoises (Gopherus agassizii) on a 1 km2 plot at Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake, California, over four survey days in September 2022: tortoise x searched 50 m cell x day, effort category per cell-day, sex and age; detector coordinates centred (CR species).
reference: Doyle, S., Murphy, S., & Esque, T. (2025). Spatially explicit demographics of Mojave desert tortoises on a demography plot in California. Herpetologica.
notes: SCR (E9 experimental) with discretised search-track detectors and effort categories as secr usage. Detector coordinates centred on the grid (IUCN CR). First reptile SCR table.

notes: Unit = season x station (station codes are per season). Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Camera-trap detection of Eurasian lynx, European wildcat and grey wolf in 14-day sessions at 140 stations in the Southern Carpathians, Romania, winter 2018/19 and autumn 2019, with effort and landscape covariates.

description: American marten camera-trap detection/non-detection at 197 stations in Maine over seven summer/winter seasons of 33 occasions each (station activity varies by season: 197 active in S1, 26 in S4); no covariates or coordinates deposited.

notes: Occasion length and calendar years not stated in the deposit; seasons labelled S1-S4 / W1-W3 in __periods. No associated paper DOI on the deposit.

description: Daily capture histories of 842 individually marked false heath fritillaries (557 males, 285 females) over 25 search days in 14 mapped search areas at Siitama, Finland, 1995, with the area of each capture and the areas searched each day.

description: Camera-trap community data for 18 mammal species at 138 stations in cattle-grazed temperate forest along the China-Russia border, Northeast China: per station x species the number of 14-day windows with a detection and the number of windows surveyed (binomial_count), with 12 site covariates as deposited; no coordinates.

description: Black-and-white Warbler point counts at 272 sites in Macon County, North Carolina (2010 or 2011), three visits each, with every visit coded 0 not detected / 1 unconfirmed detection / 2 confirmed detection; site coordinates, percent forest within 200 m and survey year as covariates. description: Session-level capture histories of 684 introduced feral cats over 196 trapping sessions at three sites on Grande Terre, Kerguelen Islands, 1994-2013, with sex, body condition and session dates.

description: Mist-net detection / non-detection of 42 bat species at 18 forest and farmland sites (6 coffee) in southern Costa Rica, 2009-2013 (185 netting visits, one to three per site per year), with coffee, terrain and tree-cover covariates.

description: Detection/non-detection of 74 fish species in 100 HUC12 watersheds of the Upper and Middle New River basin (Virginia/North Carolina) across 25 surveyed three-year primary periods of a 26-period grid (1938-2014; __periods carries all 26), compiled from collection records; years within a period are secondary occasions and the number of collections per HUC-year is the effort covariate.

description: Twelve years (2001-2012) of dry- and wet-season bird surveys on 44 transects in forest, diversified and intensive agriculture across four regions of Costa Rica (Frishkoff et al. 2014, Science): surveys with a detection out of three per transect x season x taxon, 490 taxa (486 species, 4 genus-only records), with land use and region.

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of guigna, Molina's hog-nosed skunk, foxes (Lycalopex), domestic dog and domestic cat at 180 grid-cell camera stations over up to 14 five-night occasions in agricultural landscapes of La Araucania, Chile (2019), with camera nights and human detections per occasion and 13 landscape metrics per station.

description: Open-population spatial capture-recapture of tigers at Nagarahole Reserve, India (WCS, 1991-2000): 75 photo-identified individuals x 193 camera stations active in at least one period (195 deposited) x 10 primary periods, y = trap days with a capture per station-period, effort = active trap days; station coordinates centred by the authors (local metres).

description: Annual multistate encounter histories (pre-breeder / breeder / non-breeder) of 2,734 known-age echo parakeets ringed as nestlings in Mauritius (1994-2021 cohorts), one state per breeding season 1994-2022; rows from the ringing season.

description: Calling index (0 none to 3 full chorus) of 14 frog and toad species inside the study plot on 2,216 night-time site visits at 70 Atchafalaya Basin sites, Louisiana (2008-2016), with the outside-plot index as a covariate, survey conditions, observers and site coordinates.

description: Counts of 47 amphibian and reptile species on 2,216 night-time time-constrained visual encounter surveys at 70 sites in the Atchafalaya Basin, Louisiana (2008-2016; 4-6 samples per site-year), with survey duration, weather and water variables, observers, and site coordinates.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H., 2025, Data from time-constrained visual encounter surveys and acoustic surveys for amphibians and reptiles in the Atchafalaya Basin conducted from 2008 through 2016: U.S. Geological Survey data release.

description: Koala and central greater glider spotlight detection/non-detection at 34 road transects in Richmond Range National Park, NSW, three surveys per year for eight years (2014-2021; 20 to 34 transects over time), with seven deposited habitat covariates; multi-season occupancy design spanning the 2019 drought.

notes: Cluster-level detection per census; female-phascogale file and camera study not shipped.

description: Dependent double-observer helicopter counts of waterfowl flocks (15 duck and goose species) on 27 plots in Labrador, Canada, June 2009: flocks detected by the primary observer pair and flocks missed by them but detected by the secondary pair, with plot area, observer position and experience.
